main_body: A flat wall face (metal/panel wall) with an orange trim band at row 5-6, recessed panels with shelves and a vent grille, and a lower baseboard with rails. It is drawn as a flat front-facing wall.
top_band: none; the orange band at rows 5-6 is a 1-2px trim line, and the blue-grey rows 0-4 are the wall face
evidence: The kind is terrain (wall face autotile), which is drawn as a flat front-facing surface. The column scan shows an outline, a flat blue-grey wall, a 1-row orange trim line and then panels with no horizontal top surface. There is no top band wider than 1-2 rows. The panels have inset edges, but the whole piece is a vertical wall face seen straight on, i.e. a front elevation. As a wall face tile this is acceptable for terrain, but under the strict contract there is no visible top surface, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has 14 distinct colours against 33 for the stone reference and 68 for the timber reference. Its median of 9 colours per tile is below the stone reference (13) and well below the timber reference (26). Its outlines are tinted (0% neutral dark edge pixels), so they read as dark material tone rather than a sticker line. Shading is shallow, about 4 steps of blue-grey with a few orange and brown steps. Panels have large, mostly flat areas with only a few highlight dots and rivets, and no grain or per-unit texture. It looks thinner and flatter than the references.
